title: Portability: expose the daemon shadow projection adapter
description: Objective: land the missing production new-side adapter that task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 needs to compare copied legacy state against the daemon without a test helper inventing current truth. Add the real apps/daemon -> @moe/import dependency edge, capture one durable store horizon, derive the versioned read-only CLAIM/LINK/BLOCKER ShadowProjection only from shipped daemon readers/events, and fail closed wherever a semantic current fact is absent or unverifiable. This is a pure read adapter; it must never mutate or activate anything.
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/package.json declares @moe/import in dependencies, pnpm-lock.yaml carries the apps/daemon importer link, and a compiled probe inside apps/daemon imports the public bare @moe/import root and typechecks before the probe is deleted.

A focused production adapter captures one SqliteEventStore horizon and returns a deeply frozen moe-shadow-projection/1 value whose CLAIM, LINK, and BLOCKER entities are derived only from real daemon durable readers/events; unavailable semantics refuse with an exact stable code and layer rather than being fabricated from BoardProjection counts or caller bytes.

The adapter canonicalizes entity ids, fields, and ordering so unchanged durable bytes serialize identically; malformed, ambiguous, horizon-drifted, unsupported, and unreadable evidence each fail closed with their exact code/layer and no partial projection.

The production consumer invokes public compareShadowProjections with the adapter result; neither the test nor @moe/import reimplements the daemon mapping, and all comparison results remain advisory-only with no command affordance.

Real SqliteEventStore tests assert one accepted nonempty CLAIM control, explicit behavior for unavailable LINK/BLOCKER facts, a positive hostile/refusal case count, exact reason code/layer, and unchanged raw event/decision counts plus database bytes/mtime across every read.

Use TDD; every refusal test asserts exact stable reason code and refusing layer, generated matrices assert nonzero cases, and a mutation of the production mapper must redden a named assertion.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the reader skeleton in apps/daemon/src/projections/import-shadow-reader.ts plus its bridge — an EXACT one-line LF file `export * from "./import-shadow-reader.ts";` (every production .ts in this tree has one; without it the module is invisible to consumers while tsc and vitest both stay green).
`readImportShadowProjection(store, { manifestDigest })`, in this order:
1. `store.readEventHorizon()` in try/catch -> IMPORT_SHADOW_STORE_UNREADABLE. ONE horizon, captured before any read.
2. `store.readEvents(`legacy-import:${manifestDigest}`)` in try/catch -> IMPORT_SHADOW_STORE_UNREADABLE; zero events -> IMPORT_SHADOW_ABSENT. The caller names WHICH import; it never supplies a fact. That is the same posture `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` takes with `effectId` — the identifier locates, the durable bytes decide.
3. Per event, in aggregateSequence order: sequence must equal index+1 (hole or reorder -> IMPORT_SHADOW_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED); eventType must match the `legacy.<kind>.imported` shape (anything else -> IMPORT_SHADOW_EVENT_UNSUPPORTED); the envelope's `domainSchemaVersion` must equal `IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION` (-> IMPORT_SHADOW_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED). Step 1(b) is what makes this check meaningful rather than a check against a default nobody set.
4. Decode with public `decodeImportEventFacts(event.payload)`. A refusal is returned with its OWN `IMPORT_EVENT_*` code and its OWN layer verbatim — never restamped into a local code. The seven upstream codes already distinguish malformed bytes, noncanonical bytes, incomplete facts, unknown field, identity conflict, schema conflict and schema unsupported; duplicating them locally would create two vocabularies that drift.
5. Cross-check `facts.shadowVersion === SHADOW_PROJECTION_VERSION` and `facts.claim.provenance.manifestDigest === manifestDigest` -> IMPORT_SHADOW_BINDING_MISMATCH otherwise. A row whose provenance names a different manifest is not this import's row.
6. Re-read the horizon after the scan; if it moved -> IMPORT_SHADOW_HORIZON_DRIFT with NO partial projection. A projection assembled across a moving horizon is a mixture of two states.
Every refusal is deeply frozen with `ok:false`, `advisoryOnly:true`, `authority:"NONE"`, its code, its refusing layer, and no entities field at all — a partial projection must be unrepresentable, not merely unproduced.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the DAEMON MAPPER — the independent production mapping from decoded facts to ShadowEntity[]. Keep it in import-shadow-reader.ts if that file stays under 250 physical lines; if not, split it into apps/daemon/src/projections/import-shadow-mapper.ts plus its exact one-line LF bridge (authorized by this plan; the per-FILE cap is hard).
THE MAPPING MUST BE INDEPENDENT, and that is the point of the whole task: `projectLegacyImport` maps the LEGACY side, and calling it here too would make the shadow comparison compare a function with itself and report perfect agreement forever. Write the daemon's own mapping:
- CLAIM: id = `claim.claimId`; fields = { principal: claim.principal, sourcePath: claim.provenance.sourcePath, status: claim.status } — exactly the three names `SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS.CLAIM` declares, all as canonical text.
- BLOCKER: emitted ONLY for a SUSPENDED claim; fields = { basis: "SUSPENDED_CLAIM", holder: claim.principal }. A HISTORICAL claim emits none, and that absence is a fact rather than a gap.
- LINK: id = SHA-256 over canonical ordered JSON `{from, kind, to, version}`; fields = { evidenceOnly, from, kind, to }, with `evidenceOnly` rendered as canonical text since every ShadowEntity field value is text.
- ORDER: sort by kind in code-unit order, then by id. Unchanged durable bytes must serialize identically across runs, so the order is total and derived, never insertion order.
A field outside the declared vocabulary is never emitted — the comparator reports unmapped fields as UNKNOWN, and emitting one here would launder a daemon-invented field into a comparison. Do NOT reach for BoardProjection, its byType counts, or WorkClaimLedger for any of this (task rail 2): a count is not a semantic fact, and agreement manufactured from one is the exact failure this adapter exists to prevent.

INDEPENDENCE — the point of the whole task, and MEASURED not asserted:
`grep -n "projectLegacyImport|BoardProjection|WorkClaimLedger|byType"` across all three new production files returns THREE hits, ALL of them inside the mapper's header COMMENT explaining why it does not reach for them. Zero code hits. The mapper's entire import list is `node:crypto` createHash plus `SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS`, `SHADOW_PROJECTION_VERSION` and four types from `@moe/import` — the published CONTRACT, never the legacy walk. It cannot reach `projectLegacyImport` transitively either: there is no shared helper between them, because the daemon computes its own digest and its own comparator.

THE MAPPING:
- CLAIM: id = claim.claimId; fields keyed off SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS.CLAIM[0..2] themselves (principal, sourcePath from provenance, status) rather than off hand-typed string literals, so a contract rename cannot leave this file silently emitting a stale field name.
- BLOCKER: emitted ONLY when claim.status === "SUSPENDED"; fields keyed off SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS.BLOCKER[0..1] = {basis: "SUSPENDED_CLAIM", holder: claim.principal}. Derived from the claim's own status so it cannot outlive it; a HISTORICAL claim emits none and that absence is a FACT.
- LINK: id = SHA-256 over the canonical sorted-key JSON `{"from":..,"kind":..,"to":..,"version":"moe-shadow-projection/1"}`, digested over the TUPLE rather than a joined key (from "a"+to "b:c" and from "a:b"+to "c" both render as a:b:c and would silently merge two distinct links). fields keyed off SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS.LINK[0..3]; evidenceOnly rendered with String() because every ShadowEntity field value is canonical TEXT.
- ORDER: `sort(compareEntities)` = byCodeUnit(kind) then byCodeUnit(id). Total and derived; insertion order is never consulted. byCodeUnit is local and deliberately not localeCompare, whose result varies with host ICU data.

No field outside SHADOW_ENTITY_FIELDS is ever emitted — the comparator reports an undeclared field as UNKNOWN, so emitting one would launder a daemon-invented field into a comparison as though both sides had agreed to it. No clock, no random source, no store, no port.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the PRODUCTION COMPARISON ENTRY POINT — DoD item 4. Export a second function from the same module, e.g. `compareImportShadow(store, { manifestDigest }, legacyFacts)`, which:
1. projects the LEGACY side through public `projectLegacyImport(legacyFacts)` — the importer's own mapping, not a copy;
2. reads the CURRENT side through `readImportShadowProjection` — the daemon's independent mapping from step 4;
3. compares them through public `compareShadowProjections(legacy, current)` — @moe/import's own comparator, never a local diff.
A refusal from either side short-circuits and is returned with its own code and layer; the comparison never runs over a half-built side.
The wrapper is deeply frozen and carries `advisoryOnly: true` and `authority: "NONE"`, and it exposes NO command affordance — no commit, no activate, no cutover, no "best tool" decision, and no method that could be mistaken for one. `ShadowComparison` already disposes every mismatch as NEEDS_RECONCILIATION or UNKNOWN and has no third arm; nothing here may widen that.
This function is what keeps the mapping in production rather than in the suite: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 calls THIS, so neither it nor @moe/import reimplements the daemon side.
